Emerging technologies in cryogenics,
superconductivity, and aerospace increasingly rely on fluids such as liquid
nitrogen (LN2), liquid hydrogen (LH2), and liquid oxygen (LO2), which operate at
extremely low temperatures.

This advancement is expected to
markedly improve the design, safety, and performance of cryogenic thermal
management systems.
